newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa stable but heart problem persists.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa stable but heart problem persists.

text.p: Mother Teresa's condition was stable on Monday after an uneasy night of chest pains and lung congestion, but doctors treating the revered nun said she might have to undergo a surgical procedure.
"Mother Teresa had mild chest pain early this morning," a medical bulletin issued by a panel of doctors treating the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun said. "Otherwise her condition remains unchanged."
Doctors at the Woodlands Nursing Home in Calcutta, where Mother Teresa is being treated, said her condition stabilised after her third heart failure in four days occurred on Sunday.
But Mother Teresa's condition remained precarious.
"At the moment her condition is stable. But her condition can turn bad any moment. She is not out of danger," said Dr S. K. Sen, the hospital's medical director.
Sen said the doctors were considering the possibility of surgery to relieve Mother Teresa.
"Now we have to do some invasive cardiology," he said.

One possible treatment might be angioplasty, in which doctors insert a balloon into blood vessels to clear them of obstructions, Sen said. Mother Teresa was reluctant to have any invasive cardiology, he added.
"We have to talk to the nuns of the Missionaries of Charity and then we have to approach her for her consent. Only then can we find out if she needs an angioplasty or not," he said.
Sen said the missionary woke up at about 10.30 a.m. (0500 GMT) and, when asked if she had slept well, replied, "Yes".

Known as the "Saint of the Gutters" for her work with the world's downtrodden, Mother Teresa was admitted to hospital with an irregular heart beat early on Friday. It was the third time since August she had been admitted for emergency care.
The Nobel Peace Prize winner had begun recovering on Saturday and told doctors she wanted to go home.
But she suffered left ventricular heart failure on Saturday night and again on Sunday morning.
"Her rate of progress is very slow," Sen said. "She has chest pain and heart failure because of lung congestion."
Mother Teresa was in the intensive cardiac unit, Sen said. Her problem had been checked with medication. She was under sedation and sleeping.
"She is better. She is talking. She is obeying her doctors," said Father Michael, a British priest who visited her briefly. "We are all praying for her recovery."
Fitted with a heart pacemaker in 1989, Mother Teresa has spent time in hospital for heart disease, bacterial pneumonia, broken ribs, malaria and lung problems.
Mother Teresa received honorary American citizenship, one of only five people in U.S. history, in a ceremony led by U.S. Ambassador to India Frank Wisner on November 16.
She began her life's work in the slums of Calcutta, India's most densely populated city, in 1949.
